answer.known_results: MasakhaNER is a named-entity recognition benchmark for 10 African languages; fine-tuned multilingual transformers like AfroXLMR/XLM-R typically achieve F1 in the 80s-90s on most languages, with strong cross-lingual transfer results reported.

A challenging Text-to-SQL benchmark with databases like superhero, california_schools, and codebase_community plus external evidence hints; even top LLMs like GPT-4 achieve only ~50-60% execution accuracy with much lower scores for smaller models.
Frontier LLMs achieve high pass rates on Exercism-style coding exercises, with GPT-4 and similar models solving a large majority of introductory tasks in Python and C++.
Top frontier LLMs now score ~88-92% on MMLU while GPT-4 was ~86% and earlier models like GPT-3.5 were around 70%, with near saturated performance on many subsets.

BIRD is a challenging large-scale text-to-SQL benchmark; top LLMs/GPT-4-based systems achieve roughly 60-70% execution accuracy, well below human performance, with difficulty on external knowledge and complex schemas.

BBQ tests social biases in QA; state-of-the-art LLMs score well on disambiguated contexts but show significant stereotyped biases and degraded accuracy on ambiguous contexts, with bias scores varying by category.

Belebele is a multilingual parallel reading-comprehension benchmark covering 122 languages; frontier LLMs score ~90%+ on English but significantly lower on low-resource languages like Sepedi/Northern Sotho.
CRUXEval tests code execution reasoning (input-prediction and output-prediction); top models like GPT-4/GPT-4o score ~50-70% while smaller code models score significantly lower.

Long-form 3-minute egocentric video QA benchmark where frontier multimodal models score well below human accuracy, with zero-shot LLMs historically around 30-40% and best multimodal systems still ~10-20 points below human performance.

BBH is a set of 23 hard tasks from BIG-Bench including causal_judgment (item 2), logical_deduction (item 1) and object_counting (item 3). With chain-of-thought prompting frontier models by 2024-2025 scored ~70-85%, well above chance but below human expert, with large gains from CoT and newer models.

BBQ measures social biases in QA across protected attributes; models show lower accuracy in ambiguous contexts and stereotyped errors, with even top LLMs showing measurable bias while recent models score ~80-90% overall.

MiniF2F is a Lean formalization of Olympiad problems (including MATH/MATHd problems). Top LLM provers achieve roughly 30-50% pass@1 with Lean 4, with recent SOTA around 50-60% using search and tool use.

SWE-Bench evaluates LLMs on resolving real GitHub issues; top frontier models in 2024-2025 resolve roughly 40-55% on SWE-Bench Verified with agentic scaffolding, with lower scores on the full original set.

answer.known_results: Public NAEP released items from nationsreportcard.gov; frontier LLMs typically score well above the Proficient level on NAEP reading and math items, often near ceiling on released grade 4/8 questions.

answer.known_results: PubMedQA is a yes/no/maybe biomedical QA benchmark; recent frontier LLMs achieve around 75-80% accuracy, with scores improving with domain fine-tuning and reasoning prompts.
MMLU is a 57-subject multiple-choice benchmark where frontier LLMs improved from ~30-40% to >85-90% accuracy, with top models now scoring around 88-92%.

tau-bench is a tool-augmented agent benchmark with retail and telecom domains requiring policy following and multi-turn tool use; frontier models score modestly with overall success rates often below 50-60%, with GPT-4 class models leading but far from perfect reliability.
